title: Lachish
lead: A fortified city of Judah in the Shephelah, Sennacherib's headquarters in 701 BC. Micah addresses it in 1:13; the siege is shown in the relief from Sennacherib's palace at Nineveh.

sections.b: Lachish is a Canaanite city taken in the conquest of Joshua (Joshua 10:31-32), a fortress of Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 11:9) and the second city of Judah in the 700s BC. In 701 BC Sennacherib besieged and took it. Hezekiah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish (2 Kings 18:14) and the Assyrian officers went from Lachish to Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17). Later the city again held out against Nebuchadnezzar (Jeremiah 34:7).
sections.refs: Joshua 10:31-32; 2 Chronicles 11:9; 2 Kings 18:14; 2 Kings 18:17; Jeremiah 34:7; Micah 1:13

sections.b: The site is Tell ed-Duweir. Ussishkin's excavations (1973 to 1994) found the Assyrian siege ramp and the destruction of the Judean city in 701 BC. Sennacherib's palace at Nineveh had a long relief of the siege, now in the British Museum, showing the ramp, the defenders and the deportation of the people.
